key_insight: A digital twin can evaluate local collective tariffs by simulating household behavior, shared metering, and tariff rules under realistic distribution-grid conditions.
engineering_relevance: The method gives engineers a practical way to test whether tariff designs reduce community costs while remaining fair and operationally plausible for residential energy communities.
method: Agent-based modeling of household load, PV generation, batteries, and EV charging
Virtual aggregation through a shared metering abstraction
Explicit tariff logic embedded in one simulation environment
evidence_signal: The abstract reports application to Danish Local Collective Tariff scenarios and finds measurable community-level cost reductions from aggregation of heterogeneous demand profiles.
watch_item: Cost neutrality can vary with the temporal alignment of consumption and generation, so tariff outcomes may be sensitive to participant behavior and local asset timing.
paper_title: A Digital Twin-Based Method for Evaluating Local Collective Tariffs in Distribution-Level Energy Systems
